# Pass criteria

The evidence genuinely straddles Experimenting and Scattered: real practice signals exist (this is NOT the tools-and-mandate case — there is an observed client-shipped prototype, a channel, secondhand reports of use), but the boundary signal — volume and spread of real generation — is exactly what the new director could not pin down ("couldn't tell me who or how often," "don't know if that was a one-off"). One verified prototype plus vague "some of them" does not establish real ongoing generation. Canonical team-ai-baseline drops to the lower stage when genuinely ambiguous, and hands the placement and the one boundary question back TOGETHER — never the question alone, and the question probes the boundary the placement rested on, not the next stage's gate.

## MUST
- Commit to a placement, and place at **Experimenting** — the floor the evidence already supports — with the one-line verdict naming the director's "Scattered" guess as not yet earned.
- Ask exactly one plain-language question probing the volume/spread boundary (essentially: is this one or two people on occasional pieces, or is a real share of the team producing actual deliverables this way?) — and frame it as the single answer that would move the placement to Scattered.
- Treat the client prototype as one verified instance, not as proof of ongoing team-level generation.

## MUST NOT
- Place at Scattered on the fuzzy evidence (one prototype + "some of them" is not established volume or spread).
- Return the question(s) without committing to a placement — the fuzzy picture does not convert this into a no-score refusal, because real practice evidence exists.
- Return a general questionnaire or multiple questions.
- Ask a question about the next stage's gate (e.g. about a shared bar or Decision practice) instead of the boundary the placement rested on.
